description: Real OpenTitan Top Earl Grey gpio at the pinned revision: a TL-UL MMIO slave over the packed tl_h2d_t/tl_d2h_t struct pair, 32 filtered GPIO pads with separate output value and output-enable ports, 32 active-high level interrupts bussed through one prim_intr_hw, and a strap-sampling trigger. The declared port selection is bounded: the alert handshake arrays and the RACL policy array are outside it because the frontend cannot represent a top-level aggregate array (evidence.unknown).

resets.release: rst_ni is the single active-low reset of the gpio IP and its generated register block; every state element is written on posedge clk_i with asynchronous assertion (gpio.sv:129-134,149-162 and the prim_subreg/prim_intr_hw/prim_filter_ctr instances), so deassertion must satisfy clk_i recovery/removal timing. cio_gpio_q and cio_gpio_en_q leave reset at 0 for all 32 pads, the interrupt state and the strap registers leave reset cleared.

interrupts.hold: Bit 0 of one bussified prim_intr_hw with Width=NumIOs=32, the default FlopOutput=1 and the default IntrT("Event") (gpio.sv:170-181; prim_intr_hw.sv:39,62-70,96-102): the output is the registered level intr_gpio_o[0] = INTR_STATE[0] & INTR_ENABLE[0] and the state bit is set by the combined event for pad 0, (event_rise & INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING[0]) | (event_fall & INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING[0]) | (data_in_d[0] & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH[0]) | (~data_in_d[0] & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW[0]) (gpio.sv:183-193), with event_rise/event_fall derived from the filtered pin registered one cycle earlier (gpio.sv:75-80). It stays asserted until software clears the state bit.
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE[0] (W1C, gpio_reg_top.sv:195-220) or clear INTR_ENABLE[0]; INTR_TEST[0] can force it. The event controls (INTR_CTRL_EN_*) and the per-pad input filter (CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[0]) select which pin transitions produce the event.

port_actions.reason: Registered strap-sample output: with GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1 (the module default used by this closure) a strap_en_i pulse samples all 32 filtered pin values once per reset cycle and drives sampled_straps_o.data from reg2hw.hw_straps_data_in.q with sampled_straps_o.valid from reg2hw.hw_straps_data_in_valid.q (gpio.sv:81-107). It is a component output with no in-SoC consumer (the strap path is not instantiated), so it is exported for passive monitoring only. Note: the port is the packed struct gpio_straps_t{valid, data} (33 bits); the current renderer exports a flat logic vector, so a composition would need the struct members (see evidence.unknown).

semantics: Interrupt form, read from the RTL: gpio instantiates ONE bussified prim_intr_hw with Width=NumIOs=32, the default FlopOutput=1 and the default IntrT("Event") (gpio.sv:170-181; prim_intr_hw.sv:39,62-70,96-102). All 32 interrupts therefore share one W1C INTR_STATE register and one level output bus: intr_gpio_o[i] = INTR_STATE[i] & INTR_ENABLE[i], registered on clk_i, and hw2reg_intr_state_d_o = new_event | reg2hw_intr_state_q_i. This is why the profile declares 32 level sources on the single 32-bit intr_gpio_o field, each with an explicit bit index.

Interrupt events, read from the RTL: event_intr_combined = event_intr_rise | event_intr_fall | event_intr_actlow | event_intr_acthigh with event_intr_rise = event_rise & INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING, event_intr_fall = event_fall & INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING, event_intr_acthigh = data_in_d & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH and event_intr_actlow = ~data_in_d & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW (gpio.sv:183-193); event_rise = data_in_d & ~data_in_q and event_fall = ~data_in_d & data_in_q from the one-cycle-delayed filtered pin value (gpio.sv:75-80).

Pads, read from the RTL: each cio_gpio_i[i] passes through prim_filter_ctr with AsyncOn=GpioAsyncOn=1 (2-stage synchronizer), CntWidth=4 and thresh=4'hF, enabled by CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i], into data_in_d (gpio.sv:57-72), which is also what DATA_IN reads (gpio.sv:114-115). Outputs are registered: cio_gpio_o = cio_gpio_q and cio_gpio_en_o = cio_gpio_en_q (gpio.sv:119-120), updated with priority DIRECT_OUT > MASKED_OUT_UPPER > MASKED_OUT_LOWER, where a masked write only changes the enabled lanes: q <= (mask & data) | (~mask & q) (gpio.sv:122-142); the enable path is identical for DIRECT_OE / MASKED_OE_LOWER / MASKED_OE_UPPER (gpio.sv:144-162). The masked registers read their mask field back as constant 0 (assign hw2reg.masked_out_upper.mask.d = 16'h0, gpio.sv:125-128). The IP has no tristate primitive: value and enable are separate digital ports.

Strap sampling, read from the RTL: with GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, `sample_trigger = strap_en_i && !reg2hw.hw_straps_data_in_valid.q` latches data_in_d into HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN, sets HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID and drives sampled_straps_o (gpio.sv:81-93); the sample is guaranteed once per reset cycle by design. With GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0 the block is replaced by tie-offs (gpio.sv:95-111); this profile elaborates the closure's parameterization, in which the module default 1 is used.

Register map: the generated gpio_reg_pkg declares the eighteen register offsets GPIO_*_OFFSET 7'h0..7'h44 (gpio_reg_pkg.sv:229-246) inside a 7-bit address window (localparam AW = 7 in the reg_top), which is what window_size 128 records. Access and side effects are read from the generated register primitives in gpio_reg_top.sv: SwAccessW1C for INTR_STATE (gpio_reg_top.sv:198), SwAccessRW for INTR_ENABLE and the four INTR_CTRL_EN_* and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER (gpio_reg_top.sv:226,510,538,566,594,622), SwAccessRO for DATA_IN, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN (gpio_reg_top.sv:294,650,678), prim_subreg_ext with .we(intr_test_we)/.re(1'b0) for INTR_TEST and ALERT_TEST (write-only; reads return 0, gpio_reg_top.sv:254-268,274-288) and prim_subreg_ext with both .re and .we for DIRECT_OUT, MASKED_OUT_LOWER/UPPER, DIRECT_OE and MASKED_OE_LOWER/UPPER (read-write, gpio_reg_top.sv:322-336,342-375,379-412,416-432,436-469,473-506).

Bus width, integrity and byte enables, read from the pinned packages and the generated decode: top_pkg fixes TL_AW=32, TL_DW=32, TL_DBW=4, TL_SZW=2, TL_AIW=8, TL_DIW=1 and TL_AUW=23 (top_pkg.sv:8-15); the reg_top instantiates tlul_cmd_intg_chk on tl_i and tlul_rsp_intg_gen with EnableRspIntgGen=1/EnableDataIntgGen=1 on the response path (gpio_reg_top.sv:57-87), which is what integrity="required" records; tl_i.a_mask drives reg_be and each register's GPIO_PERMIT mask is checked as (|(GPIO_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be)) to raise wr_err, so per-byte write enables are honoured per register.

Clocks and resets: clk_i/rst_ni are the only clock and reset of the IP; the generated prim_subreg blocks, the prim_filter_ctr instances, the interrupt primitive and the output registers are all posedge clk_i with rst_ni (asynchronous assertion), and the elaborated port list has no second clock.

Each declared capability and the construct it was read from: address_width=32, data_width=32, size_width=2, source_width=8, sink_width=1 and user_width=23 are the pinned top_pkg constants TL_AW/TL_DW/TL_SZW/TL_AIW/TL_DIW/TL_AUW (top_pkg.sv:8-15), which are the widths of the tl_i/tl_o struct members listed in evidence.unknown; byte_enable=true and partial_write=true are the generated decode (tl_i.a_mask drives reg_be and each register's GPIO_PERMIT mask is checked with `|(GPIO_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be)` to raise wr_err, gpio_reg_top.sv:711-778, with PutPartialData in the legal opcode set, tlul_pkg.sv:16-25); has_error=true is the d_error production of tlul_adapter_reg (d_error = error_i | err_internal with error_i = addrmiss | wr_err | intg_err, tlul_adapter_reg.sv:216-241); integrity="required" is the pair tlul_cmd_intg_chk on tl_i and tlul_rsp_intg_gen with EnableRspIntgGen=1/EnableDataIntgGen=1 on tl_o (gpio_reg_top.sv:57-87); read=true and write=true are the register read mux and the generated write paths of the reg_top; max_wait_cycles=16 is the SoC's declared patience bound (the IP completes without inserting wait states); max_outstanding=1 is the single-outstanding contract of the beat initiator and of resolve_target_adapter's parameter_values, not an RTL claim that the IP could not pipeline more.

The bus endpoint, read from the elaboration: tl_i is tlul_pkg::tl_h2d_t (109 bits) and tl_o is tlul_pkg::tl_d2h_t (66 bits); the composer's frontend reports their members with paths and bit ranges, so each of the 20 declared roles names one member (a_user and d_user name the intermediate packed structs, whose span is the union of their integrity leaves) and declares the inclusive bit range it must occupy. A declared span the elaboration contradicts is refused with member-offset-conflict, and the disposition ledger still requires all 175 bits to be classified.

The bus is driven as a real target: src/myfuzz/composition/target_adapters._resolve_tlul resolves beat-to-tlul for this profile's declared capabilities (address_width=32, data_width=32, size_width=2, source_width=8, sink_width=1, user_width=23, d_user_width=14, integrity=required, byte_enable/partial_write/has_error true), and the tl-ul plugin declares every member the adapter port list requires - a_user, d_user and d_error included - with the parameterised width expressions size_width and source_width.

d_user_width=14 is the pinned tl_d2h_t user field (rsp_intg[6:0] + data_intg[6:0]) and is the adapter's DUSER_WIDTH parameter; a_user=23 is TL_AUW (top_pkg.sv:8-15) and is USER_WIDTH. Both are declared capabilities rather than adapter constants.

sampled_straps_o is gpio_straps_t{valid, data[31:0]}, a 33-bit packed struct output. It is declared as one whole-port observation: the generated top exports it as a single 33-bit vector, which is a legal and verified packed-struct-to-vector connection, and the port is never driven by the SoC.
verified: The declared parameter set is the representable subset of the closure's: AlertSkewCycles=1 is recorded in configs/soc/closures/opentitan_gpio.json parameters and is a real top-level integer parameter of gpio (gpio.sv:13). The other recorded values - AlertAsyncOn=1'b1, GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1'b1, GpioAsyncOn=1'b1, EnableRacl=1'b0, RaclErrorRsp=1'b1 and RaclPolicySelVec='{18{1'b0}} - cannot be expressed: interface_description.ElaborationSettings accepts only decimal-integer parameter values (re.compile(r"-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\Z")), so a SystemVerilog literal such as 1'b1 or an assignment pattern is rejected as 'unsafe-elaboration-parameter' before any RTL is read. All of them take exactly those values from the module defaults and the pinned generated gpio_reg_pkg (NumIOs=32, NumAlerts=1, NumRegs=18, NumInpPeriodCounters=0, BlockAw=7), and the recorded closure command passed no -G override at all, so omitting them reproduces the recorded elaboration; AlertSkewCycles=1 is value-identical to the module default.

The declared port set, directions and widths (clk_i, rst_ni, the 32-bit intr_gpio_o, cio_gpio_i[31:0], cio_gpio_o[31:0], cio_gpio_en_o[31:0], strap_en_i, sampled_straps_o[32:0]) are the elaborated port facts of the pinned closure with those parameters, and the register offsets are the generated gpio_reg_pkg constants.

Every declared capability is carried by a semantics entry above, and the TL-UL target resolver consumes exactly address_width/data_width/byte_enable/partial_write/has_error/integrity/source_width/sink_width/user_width/size_width for this protocol.

The elaborated member layout of tl_i (13 members, 109 bits) and tl_o (11 members, 66 bits) is exactly what this profile declares: every one of the 20 endpoint roles carries a member path and the inclusive bit range that member occupies, and bind_profile re-proves each range against the frontend's own output rather than trusting it.

The endpoint is a real MMIO target: the profile's mmio_slave endpoint resolves through resolve_target_adapter to beat_to_tlul with the declared capabilities, the port-disposition ledger classifies every bit of tl_i and tl_o, and the generated top assembles the two struct ports member by member (struct_port_mapping in the independent structure audit re-reads the elaborated netlist against the plan's member-to-net record).
unknown: BLOCKER C (ports outside the bounded selection): alert_rx_i and alert_tx_o are arrays of prim_alert_pkg structs and racl_policies_i is an array of top_racl_pkg::racl_policy_t; the frontend rejects a top-level aggregate without member paths. racl_error_o is representable but omitted with them because the pinned EnableRacl=1'b0 makes the generated reg_top drive racl_error_o.valid to 0 for every access (gpio_reg_top.sv), so it carries no observable state in this parameterization. These four ports are therefore NOT elaborated, NOT classified and NOT connected; source.top_port_selection="declared" keeps this bounded selection explicit. The elaboration and the MMIO endpoint are unaffected by it.

The pinned Earlgrey integration instantiates gpio with GpioGpioAsHwStrapsEn=0 and GpioGpioAsyncOn=1 (earlgrey_pd_main.sv:1234-1238), whereas this closure elaborates the module defaults (GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, GpioAsyncOn=1). The strap-sampling behaviour described above is the behaviour of the parameterization this profile pins, not necessarily of the Earlgrey top; the composed port set is the same either way.

The register map is verified against the pinned generated bytes, not reproduced from hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/gpio/data/gpio.hjson: sources.lock.json still records the generator as regtool/topgen with status pending_input_closure_and_reproduction.

No transaction, interrupt or pad transition of this IP was simulated for this profile: the composition is verified structurally (elaborate/bind/ledger/render/audit), while MMIO protocol behaviour over time belongs to the runtime phases and is not claimed here.
